reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / KDIGO
clinicalPearls: Alport syndrome is an inherited disorder of type IV collagen affecting the basement membranes of the kidney, cochlea, and eye
The classic triad is progressive glomerular disease, sensorineural hearing loss, and characteristic ocular abnormalities such as lenticonus
Persistent microscopic haematuria, often from early childhood, is the earliest and most consistent renal finding, later accompanied by proteinuria and declining function
The most common form is X-linked, so affected males typically develop severe progressive disease while female carriers have a more variable course
A family history of haematuria, hearing loss, or renal failure across generations is an important diagnostic clue
Electron microscopy of a kidney biopsy shows characteristic splitting and lamellation of the glomerular basement membrane
Renin-angiotensin system blockade is a core management principle to reduce proteinuria and slow progression, and early treatment appears to delay kidney failure
Genetic diagnosis is increasingly used to confirm the disorder, define inheritance, and guide family screening and counselling
reference.pathophysiology: Alport syndrome arises from mutations in the genes encoding the alpha-3, alpha-4, or alpha-5 chains of type IV collagen, the principal structural component of specialised basement membranes. Defective assembly of the collagen IV network weakens the glomerular basement membrane, which progressively thickens, thins, splits, and develops the characteristic basket-weave lamellation seen on electron microscopy. The abnormal membrane cannot maintain a normal filtration barrier, leading to haematuria, progressive proteinuria, glomerulosclerosis, and interstitial fibrosis. Because the same collagen chains are found in the cochlea and the lens and retina, the disorder also produces sensorineural hearing loss and ocular changes. Inheritance is most often X-linked, with autosomal recessive and dominant forms accounting for the remainder and influencing severity and sex distribution.
additionalDifferentials: Thin basement membrane nephropathy (benign familial haematuria)
additionalInvestigations: Urinalysis and microscopy documenting persistent haematuria and quantifying proteinuria
Audiometry to detect sensorineural hearing loss
Ophthalmological examination for lenticonus and retinal changes
Kidney biopsy with electron microscopy of the glomerular basement membrane
Genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis and define the inheritance pattern
Family screening for haematuria and hearing loss
redFlags: Emergence of proteinuria and rising creatinine signalling progression toward kidney failure
Rapidly worsening renal function suggesting a superimposed process
Acute visual disturbance from ocular complications
reference.prognosis: In classic X-linked disease, affected males commonly progress to end-stage kidney disease by early to middle adulthood, whereas female carriers and some autosomal forms have a more variable and often milder course. Early renin-angiotensin blockade can delay progression. Transplantation is generally successful, though a small number of patients develop anti-GBM disease in the graft against the previously absent collagen antigen.
pitfalls: Dismissing persistent childhood haematuria as benign without a family and hearing assessment
Confusing Alport syndrome with thin basement membrane nephropathy on light microscopy alone
Delaying renin-angiotensin blockade until proteinuria is advanced
Overlooking the small post-transplant risk of anti-GBM disease in affected recipients
management: Initiate renin-angiotensin system blockade with an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker early to reduce proteinuria and delay end-stage kidney disease
Monitor blood pressure, proteinuria and eGFR and manage chronic kidney disease complications such as anaemia and mineral-bone disorder
Provide audiological surveillance with hearing aids for sensorineural hearing loss
Arrange ophthalmology review for lenticonus and retinal changes
Plan timely renal replacement therapy including dialysis and transplantation, monitoring transplant recipients for anti-glomerular basement membrane disease
Offer genetic counselling, define the inheritance pattern, and screen at-risk relatives for haematuria and hearing loss
